arxiv-2111-05950.title: Self-Compression in Bayesian Neural Networks
arxiv-2111-05950.description: Abstract Machine learning models have achieved human-level performance on various tasks. This success comes at a high cost of computation and storage overhead, which makes machine learning algorithms difficult to deploy on edge devices. Typically, one has to partially sacrifice accuracy in favor of an increased performance quantified in terms of reduced memory usage and energy consumption.

arxiv-2203-02715.title: Efficient Reachability Ratio Computation for 2-hop Labeling Scheme
arxiv-2203-02715.creator: Junfeng Zhou, Xian Tang, Ming Du
arxiv-2203-02715.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Junfeng Zhou, Xian Tang, Ming Du. As one of the fundamental graph operations, reachability queries processing has been extensively studied during the past decades. Many approaches followed the line of designing 2-hop labels to make acceleration. Considering that the index size cannot be bounded when using all nodes to construct 2-hop labels, researchers proposed to use a part of important nodes to construct 2-hop labels (partial 2-hop labels) to cover as much reachability information as possible.

arxiv-2407-01774.title: Audio-Visual Approach for Multimodal Concurrent Speaker Detection Thanks: The work was partially supported by a grant from the Audition Project, Data Science Program, Council of Higher Education, Israel, and by the European Union’s Horizon 2020 Research and Innovation Programme under Grant Agreement
arxiv-2407-01774.creator: Amit Eliav, Sharon Gannot
arxiv-2407-01774.description: Abstract CSD ( CSD ), the task of identifying active speakers and their overlaps in an audio signal, is essential for various audio applications, including meeting transcription, speaker diarization, and speech separation. This study presents a multimodal deep learning approach that integrates audio and visual information.

arxiv-2503-12775.title: A study of the Antlion Random Walk
arxiv-2503-12775.creator: Akihiro Narimatsu, Tomoki Yamagami
arxiv-2503-12775.description: Abstract Random walks (RWs) are fundamental stochastic processes with applications across physics, computer science, and information processing. A recent extension, the laser chaos decision-maker, employs chaotic time series from semiconductor lasers to solve multi-armed bandit (MAB) problems at ultrafast speeds, and its threshold adjustment mechanism has been modeled as an RW.

arxiv-2510-05234.title: Emergence of nematic loop-current bond order in vanadium Kagome metals
arxiv-2510-05234.creator: Alex Friedlan, Hae-Young Kee
arxiv-2510-05234.description: Abstract The family of layered Kagome metals AV 3 ​ Sb 5 \mathrm{A}\mathrm{V}_{3}\mathrm{Sb}_{5} ( A = K , Rb , Cs ) (\mathrm{A}=\mathrm{K,Rb,Cs}) has recently attracted significant interest due to reports of charge-bond order, orbital magnetism, and superconductivity. Some of these phases may exhibit time-reversal symmetry breaking, as suggested by their response to magnetic fields.

arxiv-2512-16108.title: WeMusic-Agent: Efficient Conversational Music Recommendation via Knowledge Internalization and Agentic Boundary Learning
arxiv-2512-16108.creator: Wendong Bi
arxiv-2512-16108.description: Abstract Personalized music recommendation in conversational scenarios usually requires a deep understanding of user preferences and nuanced musical context, yet existing methods often struggle with balancing specialized domain knowledge and flexible tool integration. This paper proposes WeMusic-Agent, a training framework for efficient LLM-based conversational music recommendation.

arxiv-2602-00370.title: POET : Protocol Optimization via Eligibility Tuning
arxiv-2602-00370.creator: Trisha Das, Katherine Kero, Dorinda Schumann, Tracy Ohrt, Sanjit Singh Batra, Gregory D Lyng, Robert E. Tillman

arxiv-2602-03421.title: On (Im)possibility of Network Oblivious Transfer via Noisy Channels and Non-Signaling Correlations
arxiv-2602-03421.creator: Hadi Aghaee, Christian Deppe, Holger Boche
arxiv-2602-03421.description: Abstract This work investigates the fundamental limits of implementing network oblivious transfer via noisy multiple access channels and broadcast channels between honest-but-curious parties when the parties have access to general tripartite non-signaling correlations. By modeling the shared resource as an arbitrary tripartite non-signaling box, we obtain a unified perspective on both the channel behavior and the resulting correlations.

pmc-10485005.title: Contactless deformation of fluid interfaces by acoustic radiation pressure
pmc-10485005.creator: Félix Sisombat, Thibaut Devaux, Lionel Haumesser, Samuel Callé
pmc-10485005.description: Reversible and programmable shaping of surfaces promises wide-ranging applications in tunable optics and acoustic metasurfaces. Based on acoustic radiation pressure, contactless and real-time deformation of fluid interface can be achieved. This paper presents an experimental and numerical study to characterize the spatiotemporal properties of the deformation induced by acoustic radiation pressure.

pmc-11358447.title: Trifunctional sphingomyelin derivatives enable nanoscale resolution of sphingomyelin turnover in physiological and infection processes via expansion microscopy
pmc-11358447.creator: Marcel Rühling, Louise Kersting, Fabienne Wagner, Fabian Schumacher, Dominik Wigger, Dominic A Helmerich, Tom Pfeuffer, Robin Elflein, Christian Kappe, Markus Sauer, Christoph Arenz, Burkhard Kleuser, Thomas Rudel, Martin Fraunholz, Jürgen Seibel
pmc-11358447.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Sphingomyelin is a key molecule of sphingolipid metabolism, and its enzymatic breakdown is associated with various infectious diseases. Here, we introduce trifunctional sphingomyelin derivatives that enable the visualization of sphingomyelin distribution and sphingomyelinase activity in infection processes. We demonstrate this by determining the activity of a bacterial sphingomyelinase on the plasma membrane of host cells using a combination of Förster resonance energy transfer and expansion microscopy.

pmc-11598478.title: An Investigation into the Viability of Portable Proximal Sensor X-Ray Fluorescence Data for Assessing Heavy Metal Contamination in Urban Soils: A Case Study in Changchun, China
pmc-11598478.creator: Xiaoxiao Zou, Jilong Lu, Xinyun Zhao, Qiaoqiao Wei, Zhiyi Gou, Yaru Hou, Yawen Lai, Samuel Caito
pmc-11598478.description: In order to validate the applicability of pXRF for rapid in situ detection of heavy metals in urban soils and to accurately obtain an assessment of soil quality in Changchun, a city in northeast China, 164 soil samples from within the main urban area of Changchun were collected for pXRF analysis.

pmc-11641082.title: The Major Domains of Comprehensive Assessment Tools for Older Adults Requiring Home-Based Aged Care Services: A Systematic Review
pmc-11641082.creator: Weiwei Fang, Hai Phung, Richard Olley, Patricia Lee, Jose Granero-Molina
pmc-11641082.description: Background/Objectives: The global population is aging rapidly, increasing the need for appropriate health care. Older people often prefer to remain in their homes for as long as possible as they age. Therefore, it is crucial to assess their overall health and understand the individualized care needs for developing tailored home care services.

pmc-11674932.title: Conservation of structural brain connectivity in people with multiple sclerosis
pmc-11674932.creator: Gerard Martí-Juan, Jaume Sastre-Garriga, Angela Vidal-Jordana, Sara Llufriu, Eloy Martinez-Heras, Sergiu Groppa, Gabriel González-Escamilla, Maria A. Rocca, Massimo Filippi, Einar A. Høgestøl, Hanne F. Harbo, Michael A. Foster, Sara Collorone, Ahmed T. Toosy, Menno M. Schoonheim, Eva Strijbis, Giuse
pmc-11674932.description: Multiple sclerosis (MS) is a neurodegenerative disease that affects the central nervous system. Structures affected in MS include the corpus callosum, connecting the hemispheres. Studies have shown that in mammalian brains, structural connectivity is organized according to a conservation principle, an inverse relationship between intra- and interhemispheric connectivity.

pmc-11726222.title: Relationship between Helicobacter pylori infection and gastroesophageal reflux disease
pmc-11726222.creator: Seda Yılmaz, Kadir Gisi, Ali Cetinkaya, Bulent Kantarceken, Harun Ciralik
pmc-11726222.description: IntroductionGastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD) is a common disease that negatively affects the quality of life, and its pathophysiology is multifactorial.AimOur study aims to investigate the relationship between histological and topographic characteristics of Helicobacter pylori (H. pylori) gastritis and the symptoms, presence, and severity of oesophagitis in patients with reflux symptoms.

pmc-12470128.title: Whey: Composition, Processing, Application, and Prospects in Functional and Nutritional Beverages—A Review
pmc-12470128.creator: Assiya Mirzakulova, Tolkyn Sarsembaeva, Zhulduz Suleimenova, Łukasz Kowalski, Bożena Gajdzik, Radosław Wolniak, Michał Bembenek
pmc-12470128.description: Whey is a byproduct of dairy production that possesses high nutritional value and versatile applications across various industries. In the framework of circular economy, the reutilization of whey is essential to transform this high-volume byproduct into a valuable resource. In this narrative review, the authors focus on trends in the utilization of whey for manufacturing functional and nutritional beverages.

pmc-12650854.title: Learning in Probabilistic Boolean Networks via Structural Policy Gradients
pmc-12650854.creator: Pedro Juan Rivera Torres
pmc-12650854.description: We revisit Probabilistic Boolean Networks as trainable function approximators. The key obstacle, non-differentiable structural choices (which predictors to read and which Boolean operators to apply), is addressed by casting the PBN’s structure as a stochastic policy whose parameters are optimized with score-function (REINFORCE) gradients. Continuous output heads (logistic/linear/softmax or policy logits) are trained with ordinary gradients.

pmc-13006133.title: Consensus Statement on Practical Guidance for Optimizing Antihypertensive Therapy in Older Adults Needing Nursing Care by the Japan Geriatrics Society and the Japanese Society of Hypertension: English Translation of the Japanese Article
pmc-13006133.creator: Yoshio Iwashima, Yuichi Akasaki, Norihisa Ito, Yoichi Nozato, Yoichi Takami, Jiro Okochi, Kei Kamide, Koichi Yamamoto
pmc-13006133.description: This Consensus Statement outlines management for nursing care‐dependent older adults (Categories 3–4). Key principles include prioritizing QOL over strict BP targets, avoiding reduction of SBP < 120 mmHg, and implementing stepwise deprescribing. It also emphasizes safety protocols during bathing and rehabilitation to prevent adverse event.

pmc-13031386.title: Mismatched parameters selection and error sensitivity analysis of easy-off TEC worm drive
pmc-13031386.creator: Chongfei Huai, Shenghai Sun, Jingtian Gai, Zifei Wang
pmc-13031386.description: This paper establishes a geometric model of easy-off Toroidal Enveloping Conical (TEC) worm drive that incorporates errors, and based on this, investigates the influence of mismatched parameters on the tooth contact performance and the sensitivity to errors of this type of worm pair.

pmc-13048399.title: Purple Urine Bag Syndrome in the Setting of a Percutaneous Nephrostomy: Case Report and Review of the Literature
pmc-13048399.creator: Sarah Griffin, Mary Moore, Alexa Lapointe, Hannah Zulli, Shane Guillory
pmc-13048399.description: Purple Urine Bag Syndrome (PUBS) is an uncommonly described entity in which purple discoloration of urine can be seen in patients with recurrent urinary tract infection or bacterial colonization. It most commonly affects patients with chronic indwelling foley catheters and those who are chronically debilitated. Reports of PUBS affecting patients with percutaneous nephrostomy tubes are even less common.

pmc-13241893.title: Letter to the editor in response to “Rare presentation of lues maligna and nodular syphilis in an immunocompetent patient”
pmc-13241893.creator: Tarun Narang, Sejal Jain, Bhushan Kumar
pmc-13241893.description: uestion the classification as lues maligna (LM), the treatment regimen, and certain other interpretations. LM is a rare ulceronodular variant of SS characterised by rapidly progressive painful, necrotic “punched-out” ulcers with dark rupioid crusts and erythematous halos, often associated with immunosuppression.

pmc-13588521.title: Therapeutic potential of haptoglobin in a murine model of sickle cell anemia
pmc-13588521.creator: Bianca Cristina dos Santos, Magnun Nueldo Nunes dos Santos, Gisele Audrei Pedroso, Beatriz Benedetti de Oliveira, Dulcinéia Martins de Albuquerque, Nathalia Rocha de Oliveira, Daniela Cagnoto Noronha, Fernando Ferreira Costa, Marcus Alexandre Finzi Corat, Fábio Silva, Fábio Silva, Fábio Silva, Fábio
pmc-13588521.description: Chronic hemolytic anemia found in patients with sickle cell disease promotes an excess of free extracellular and intravascular hemoglobin, triggering a series of deleterious effects such as endothelial dysfunction, oxidative stress, and alterations in vascular tone, which lead to clinical complications.

pmc-13692691.title: Completion, publication, and outcome reporting of registered randomized trials in abdominal surgery: registry-based cohort study
pmc-13692691.creator: Klaudia Narbekovas, Christoph Kuemmerli, Sandro Huegli, Jasper P Sijberden, Lukas W Widmer, Oliver Strobel, Max F Stauffer, Ethan B Ludmir, Carl-Stephan Leonhardt
pmc-13692691.description: BackgroundAbdominal surgery poses unique challenges to the conduct of randomized clinical trials (RCTs). However, trial discontinuation, non-publication, and selective reporting may result in an incomplete picture of the available evidence base. This study assessed the trajectories of RCTs in abdominal surgery from trial registration to the publication and reporting of results.

pmc-7617530.title: Protein structural context of cancer mutations reveals molecular mechanisms and candidate driver genes
pmc-7617530.creator: Diego Chillón-Pino, Mihaly Badonyi, Colin A Semple, Joseph A Marsh
pmc-7617530.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). SummaryAdvances in protein structure determination and modeling allow us to study the structural context of human genetic variants on an unprecedented scale. Here, we analyze millions of cancer-associated missense mutations based on their structural locations and predicted perturbative effects. By considering the collective properties of mutations at the level of individual proteins, we identify distinct patterns associated with tumor suppressors and oncogenes.
